opening_brief.intro: 本期首看《The (missing) gamma-ray counterparts to EP events》等 22 篇核心进展。

must_read.label: The (missing) gamma-ray counterparts to EP events
must_read.text: 样本中68%（49/72）的EP源无伽马射线对应体，X射线时延持续时间显著长于伽马射线（$T_{\rm 100,X\text{-}ray}/T_{90} \sim 12$）。

must_read.label: Double-Shock Radiation in Supernova Wind Breakout and EP260321a
must_read.text: 推导了双激波结构中内能比 $E_3 = \mu E_2$ 与特征速度比 $\bar{v}_r = \mu v_f$（其中 $\mu = (\delta+2)^{-1} \simeq 1/7$），阐明正激波 $v_{f,bo} \sim 0.5c$ 处于非局部热平衡（non-LTE）而低速反激波 $\bar{v}_{r,bo} \sim 0.07c$ 满足 LTE 并主导黑体热辐射。

must_read.label: PSR J0653+0443: An Eclipsing Millisecond Pulsar in an Extremely Eccentric Double Neutron Star System
must_read.text: 通过 FAST 测时与近星点跟踪，测得双星轨道周期 $P_{\rm orb} = 79.0840618(1)\,{\rm d}$，偏心率高达 $e = 0.99238692(5)$，投影半长轴 $x = 125.54(3)\,{\rm lt\text{-}s}$。

opening_brief.worth_knowing_summary: 基于一维恒星演化程序 \texttt{STARS} 模拟的白矮星模型，其表面磁场由 $B_s = \sqrt{\frac{3c^3}{8\pi^2}\frac{I}{R^6\sin^2\alpha}P\dot{P}}$ 约束。；混合方案将总不透明度计算耗时降低约 $8.7$ 倍，NN 前向传播比被替代的 2D 积分核快约 $12$ 倍，使端到端 BNS 模拟全局吞吐量从 $1.085\times 10^7$ 提升至 $2.347\times 10^7\,\mathrm{ZCPS}$（实现 $2.16$ 倍整体加速）。 等。
opening_brief.skim_summary: Chemical abundance patterns at z=1-7: Carbon, Nitrogen, Neon, Sulphur, and Argon abundances from JWST spectroscopy、The Balmer Absorber Strength Problem of Little Red Dots 等主题。

highlights.title: The (missing) gamma-ray counterparts to EP events
highlights.reason: 系统性分析了爱因斯坦探针（EP/WXT）首年72例河外快速X射线暂现源（FXTs）的高能（keV–GeV）伽马射线辐射特征，联合Fermi/GBM与LAT建立了严格的能谱与光度限制，直接回答了FXT是传统GRB的低能延伸、离轴观测喷流还是超新星激波破越（SBO）的核心物理疑问，契合相对论喷流与高能暂现源中心引擎研究。

highlights.title: Double-Shock Radiation in Supernova Wind Breakout and EP260321a
highlights.reason: 文章系统构建了超新星（SN）抛射物与光学厚致密周星介质（CSM）相互作用的双激波（前向激波 FS 与反向激波 RS）辐射介导激波破越（SBO）模型，并成功应用于解释爱因斯坦探针（EP）新近探测到的软 X 射线暂现源 EP260321a，高度契合本组关于激波破越、周星介质相互作用及早期高能瞬变源观测的研究方向。

highlights.title: PSR J0653+0443: An Eclipsing Millisecond Pulsar in an Extremely Eccentric Double Neutron Star System
highlights.reason: 该工作利用 FAST 发现并测时监测了迄今偏心率最高（$e = 0.99238692$）的银河系双中子星（DNS）系统 PSR J0653+0443，观测到由于近侧向轨道几何引发的伴星磁层掩食效应，精确测量后开普勒参数并限制了双星质量与非相对论进动率，对超新星反冲速度机制、双星演化通道以及极端偏心引力波暴源提供了关键物理基准。

highlights.title: Exploring the origin of slow-rotating pulsars: Emission from STARS simulated white dwarfs
highlights.reason: 文章探讨了慢自转脉冲星（SRP）及超长周期瞬变源（LPT）的白矮星（WD）假说。常规中子星模型推导出的偶极磁场系统性超过Schwinger临界场 $B_c \approx 4.41 \times 10^{13}\,\mathrm{G}$，易抑制电子对产生且落入脉冲星死区；而采用恒星演化程序模拟的磁化WD及其超钱德拉塞卡解能提供自然的自转与磁场参数匹配，有助于高能瞬变源与射电瞬变引擎的理论证认。

highlights.title: A Hybrid Neural Network Emulator for M1 Neutrino Reaction Rates in Binary Neutron Star Merger Simulations
highlights.reason: 该工作提出了一种利用轻量神经网络替代高开销 2D 积分核、同时保留解析 1D 反应的混合仿真方案，成功消除了双中子星（BNS）并合通用相对论辐射磁流体（GRMHD）模拟中灰体 M1 中微子反应率的计算瓶颈，显著提升计算吞吐量且完好保持了核合成与千新星诊断相关的电子丰度 $Y_e$ 和外流特征。

highlights.title: Exploring PSR J0901-4046 as an ultra-slowly rotating neutron star versus a white dwarf
highlights.reason: 针对超慢周期脉冲星 PSR J0901-4046 等源在中子星偶极假设下磁场过高（达 $\sim 5\times 10^{16}\text{ G}$）导致对产生受抑的理论困境，系统建立了多极电磁与非电磁减速模型，并与强磁化白矮星模型对比，为长周期射电暂现源的物理本质提供了关键理论判据。

highlights.title: The renormalization-group running of neutrino mixing is undetectable
highlights.reason: 针对近期文献声称高能中微子探测与天体物理中微子味比会随相互作用动量转移 $Q$ 发生重整化群跑动的假说，本文从场论在壳重整化角度给出了关键理论限制，证明中微子混合由质壳（$p^2 = m_i^2$）自能决定的常数矩阵 $\hat{U}$ 给出，所谓动量依赖源于不自洽截断，为高能天体中微子味比与振荡唯象学提供了重要理论约束。

highlights.title: Can we constrain the binary neutron star merger time from kilonova light curves?
highlights.reason: 文章系统量化了利用多波段千新星（KN）测光反演双中子星（BNS）并合时刻 $t_0$ 的精度与物理限制。这直接服务于无引力波（GW）触发或孤立千新星的光学后随巡天及引力波次阈值回溯搜索，切合研究组致密天体高能观测与电磁对应体物理兴趣。

highlights.title: A Comprehensive X-ray Characterization of the Pulsar Wind Nebula CTB 87: Evidence for Reverse-Shock Interaction from Its X-ray and Broadband Emissions
highlights.reason: 该工作结合 Chandra、XMM-Newton 与 NuSTAR 对脉冲星风云 CTB 87 进行了高精度 X 射线空间分辨与能谱分析，揭示了强同步冷却及内在谱曲率，并结合演化单区与多区模型探讨了反向激波压缩对粒子布居与宽波段辐射的深刻影响，为研究脉冲星风与超新星遗迹相互作用环境提供了典型观测约束与模型对比。

highlights.title: Probing the QPO and spectro-temporal evolution of MAXI J1750-327 with XPoSat during its first detected outburst : Constraints on black-hole mass and spin
highlights.reason: 该工作利用印度 XPoSat 卫星的 XSPECT 载荷，对黑洞双星瞬变源 MAXI J1750-327 首次爆发进行了谱-时联合观测，捕捉到了 Type-C 到 Type-B QPO 的演化以及截断盘向 ISCO 移动的物理过程，并基于全局 Lense-Thirring (LT) 进动模型给出了黑洞质量和自旋的定量限制，属于致密天体高能吸积与进动物理的典型观测样本研究。

highlights.title: X-ray Comptonization in an Accreting Kerr Black Hole System with a Tilted Disc and Thermal Corona: A General-Relativistic Monte Carlo Simulation. II. Polarization Signatures
highlights.reason: 该工作建立了包含 Kerr 黑洞强引力光线弯曲、Walker-Penrose 偏振平行输运、热日冕偏振康普顿散射和倾斜外吸积盘偏振反射的完整广义相对论蒙特卡罗（GRMC）偏振辐射转移模型，定量揭示了致密天体强引力弯折（增加 DOP）与多次散射/外盘发射稀释（抑制 DOP 及其进动调制）之间的竞争机制，对理解致密天体吸积系统（如黑洞 X 射线双星硬态高偏振度及 QPO 偏振调制缺失）具有重要理论和模拟价值。

highlights.title: Investigating a TeV-Halo Candidate around PSR J1928+1746 with HAWC
highlights.reason: 该工作利用 HAWC 对银道面拥挤天区的中年脉冲星 PSR J1928+1746 进行高精度空间与能谱解构，确认了覆盖 2 TeV 至 >100 TeV 的延展超额 HAWC J1928+1750，为致密天体高能观测及脉冲星周围 TeV 晕的粒子扩散抑制提供了重要实测约束。

highlights.title: Hybrid Stars with a Crossover Equation of State
highlights.reason: 文章构建了从强子到解禁夸克相（CFL模型）的平滑跨越（crossover）物态方程，放弃了传统的 Maxwell 压力平衡要求，给出了相变交叉化学势的指数标度律，并计算了混合星最大质量及潮汐形变度 $\Lambda$。该结果为超新星中心引擎致密残骸的相变软化、大质量中子星支撑以及双中子星并合引力波（如 GW170817）观测提供了核物理与致密天体微观物理约束。

highlights.title: General Relativistic Simulations of the Nonlinear Evolution of r-modes in Rapidly Rotating Neutron Stars
highlights.reason: 该工作首次在摒弃 Cowling 近似和后牛顿近似的完全广义相对论时空-流体自洽演化框架下，模拟了快速自转中子星（$f_{\rm spin} \approx 792\,\mathrm{Hz}$）中非线性 $l=|m|=2$ r 模的动力学行为，精确测定了模式频率、非线性频移、引力波应变与非线性三模耦合，为超新星后快速自转致密天体遗迹演化及连续引力波搜寻提供了基准参数约束。

highlights.title: Searches for coincident Gravitational Waves and High-Energy Neutrinos from the KM3NeT and ANTARES telescopes during O3
highlights.reason: 该工作结合LIGO/Virgo第三次观测运行（O3）以及地中海中微子望远镜ANTARES和KM3NeT/ORCA6的数据，针对高能瞬变源（如BNS、NSBH、相对论喷流及核坍缩超新星）开展了GW-HEN触发与阈下多信使联合证认，给出了辐射能量与源率密度的严格上限，与本组关于致密天体多信使高能观测和相对论喷流研究密切相关。

highlights.title: SpinOctopus: A Versatile, User-Friendly, and Extensible Public Code for General-Relativistic Ray-Tracing in axisymmetric spacetime
highlights.reason: 文章发布了一款适用于任意渐近平直、定态轴对称时空的广义相对论光线追踪与协变辐射转移开源数值工具 \texttt{SpinOctopus}，能够对黑洞双极相对论喷流、几何薄/厚吸积流及大质量粒子轨道光变进行高精度成像模拟，可为致密天体吸积系统与相对论喷流的多波段强引力场观测特征提供理论建模支持。

highlights.title: Neutron Star-Main-Sequence Star Collision: Formation and Long-Term Evolution of Thorne-Żytkow Objects
highlights.reason: 本文揭示了新生中子星与主序伴星直接碰撞形成索恩–热特科夫天体（TŻO）的自洽动力学演化及长期宿命，证实其晚期具有极强超爱丁顿脉动不稳定性，并可能伴随剧烈爆发抛射或黑洞喷流破越，为高能瞬变源与致密天体演化提供了动力学机制参考。

highlights.title: Cosmic Ray Observations using Coincident Scintillator and Radio Signals with the Beamforming Elevated Array for COsmic Neutrinos (BEACON)
highlights.reason: BEACON 旨在通过高山相控射电阵列探测超高能中微子（掠地 tau 中微子）及超高能宇宙线（UHE CR）广延空气簇射（EAS）。该工作报道了利用闪烁体阵列与 6 天线射电阵列符合探测在极低背景下成功证认 22 例宇宙线事件，展示了相干射电脉冲、电场反卷积与偏振测量技术，对高能瞬变源射电/中微子多信使探测方法有直接参考价值。

highlights.title: PBR sensitivity to boosted dark matter explanation for the KM3-230213A event
highlights.reason: 针对 KM3NeT/ARCA 探测到的超高能近水平事件 KM3-230213A（$E_\mu \sim 120\text{ PeV}$）及其超出标准模型（BSM）的增能暗物质（BDM）假说，系统评估了未来超压气球载先导实验 PBR（POEMMA-Balloon with Radio）通过掠地 $\tau$ 轻子衰变诱发的大气簇射进行探测的能力，为超高能中微子与瞬态粒子探测提供了关键的仪器灵敏度标度。

highlights.title: The diversity of late-time interaction in Type II supernovae
highlights.reason: 该工作系统研究了不同包层剥离程度的II型超新星在爆发数百天后与周星介质相互作用的辐射转移特征，阐明了冷致密壳层（CDS）物理性质与激波供能机制对紫外及光学光谱多样性的控制规律。

highlights.title: Extended vs. thin screen approximation in astrophysical settings
highlights.reason: 文章系统对比了脉冲星与 FRB 射电波在引力透镜和等离子体湍流介质中传播时全三维波动光学与薄屏近似的适用界限，首次量化了延展介质中分枝流（branched flow）对二次谱（secondary spectra）不对称闪烁弧的调制机制，对理解 FRB 闪烁微结构与周星介质层析具有直接参考价值。

highlights.title: Modeling MAD Sgr A* flares and their dependence on spin
highlights.reason: 该工作利用 3D GRMHD 模拟和 GRRT 计算，研究了磁阻滞盘（MAD）磁通量喷发事件中喷射热斑在不同自旋下的轨迹，并直接拟合 GRAVITY 对 Sgr A* 耀斑的天体测量数据，为超大质量黑洞自旋约束和相对论喷流/耀变物理提供了定量的动力学校准。

entries.title: Chemical abundance patterns at z=1-7: Carbon, Nitrogen, Neon, Sulphur, and Argon abundances from JWST spectroscopy
entries.abstract: The relative abundances of chemical elements in the interstellar medium (ISM) trace the history of star formation and chemical enrichment in galaxies. We investigate the abundance patterns of carbon (C), nitrogen (N), neon (Ne), sulfur (S), and argon (Ar) in star-forming galaxies at z=1-7, combining ultra-deep JWST/NIRSpec observations from the MARTA survey with archival spectroscopy. We assemble 244 galaxies with [OIII]4363 detections and derive direct Te-based abundances. New empirical strong-line calibrations for N/O, Ne/O, S/O, and Ar/O extend the analysis to an additional 514 galaxies. We find distinct abundance-metallicity trends. N/O is enhanced by 0.18 dex in median relative to local galaxies, with a stronger enhancement at low metallicity. Direct measurements reveal decreasing S/O and Ar/O with increasing metallicity, while strong-line measurements suggest a flattening at higher metallicities, especially for S/O. We also identify a stellar-mass dependence in the O/Ar-Ar/H plane, with lower-mass galaxies exhibiting lower O/Ar at fixed Ar/H, consistent with differences in star-formation efficiency and delayed SNe Ia enrichment. Ne/O remains approximately constant up to 12+log(O/H)=8.2, with a mild increase at higher metallicities and no significant redshift evolution. C/O tentatively increases with metallicity, broadly following the local relation. Finally, a forward model shows that observational selection affects the abundance ratios differently: it mainly restricts the accessible metallicity range for Ne/O and Ar/O, but preferentially selects galaxies with enhanced N/O at low metallicity, with a weaker effect for S/O. These results provide new constraints on chemical enrichment at high redshift and highlight the importance of accounting for selection effects when interpreting abundance-metallicity trends.

entries.title: The Balmer Absorber Strength Problem of Little Red Dots
entries.abstract: Little Red Dots (LRDs) commonly show Balmer absorption features. Some observed LRD spectra have weaker absorption in H$α$ than in H$β$, in apparent contradiction to atomic physics according to standard attenuation models. This tension is naturally resolved when one considers emission from the absorbing medium itself, which is ignored in the standard model: when the Balmer absorption is optically thick, a non-negligible source function could fill in the H$α$ absorption trough and reduce its observed absorption equivalent width (EW). With proof-of-concept photoionization models we show that the source function of H$α$ could be systematically stronger than that of H$β$. This is due to radiative trapping preferentially populating the $n=3$ level of neutral hydrogen, which operates efficiently when the medium is optically thick to H$α$ but not very optically thick to Paschen-$α$. Such line-dependent source functions could lead to significant corrections to the expected EW and selectively weaken H$α$ absorption, consistent with observations. Quantitatively, this depends on the distance of the absorbing medium and its internal structure, providing a new diagnostic of the environment around LRDs. Future modeling of the absorbers may also potentially open a new avenue for estimating the mass of the central engine.

entries.title: Arepo-CD: Coupling Collisional $N$-Body Dynamics with Moving-Mesh Magnetohydrodynamics
entries.abstract: Star formation is a hierarchical, clustered process in turbulent giant molecular clouds (GMCs), where close stellar encounters can strongly affect cluster evolution and feedback. However, gravitational softening in many hydrodynamic simulations of GMCs limits the treatment of these encounters. We present Arepo-CD (Collisional Dynamics), a framework that couples star-by-star collisional $N$-body dynamics to the moving-mesh magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) code Arepo. Star-star interactions use unsoftened gravity, while interactions involving gas or collisionless components remain softened. Compact stellar subsystems are identified on the fly and evolved with a fourth-order forward symplectic integrator and slow-down algorithmic regularization coupled to the native Arepo timestep hierarchy. Benchmark tests against the collisional $N$-body code PeTar show good agreement in cluster core collapse and subsequent expansion, radial density profiles, and stellar velocity distributions. Coupled to the Rigel star formation and feedback model, Arepo-CD follows cluster formation and early evolution in radiation MHD simulations of a $10^5~M_\odot$ turbulent molecular cloud. In the fiducial GMC comparison, the collisional and softened-gravity runs yield similar star formation histories and integrated star formation efficiencies. Nevertheless, close gravitational encounters during the embedded phase generate a substantial runaway population, with a velocity tail extending beyond 100 km/s. Ejected massive stars redistribute radiative feedback into the surrounding lower-density medium and produce a more extended distribution of heated gas. Arepo-CD provides a practical and computationally efficient framework for studying collisional stellar dynamics and its coupling to gas evolution and feedback during star cluster formation in realistic galactic environments.

entries.title: Exploring the origin of slow-rotating pulsars: Emission from STARS simulated white dwarfs
entries.abstract: An increasing number of slow-rotating pulsars and long-period transients have been observed in recent years. The periods of these sources can be significantly longer than typical pulsar sources, ranging from ~ 100 - 1000 s, or even longer. The observed periods and period derivatives predict high magnetic fields, higher than the Schwinger field, when we consider conventional pulsar models of dipole-driven emission from neutron stars. Interestingly, the periods of these sources are consistent with the current observations of white dwarfs (WDs). We explore the possibility of magnetic WDs, simulated using the stellar evolution code STARS, as the origin of some of these unusual pulsar observations. We simulate WDs with enhanced magnetic fields due to accretion after their formation. We also briefly touch on the more exotic possibility of super-Chandrasekhar WDs as the origin for these sources. We find that expanding the parameter space to include the possibility of a WD origin provides an alternate and viable explanation for these unusual observations.

entries.title: Simulation-Informed High-Velocity Dark Matter in the Effective Theory of Direct Detection
entries.abstract: The interpretation and reach of direct detection (DD) experiments depend sensitively on the local dark matter (DM) velocity distribution, particularly its high-velocity tail. This tail is crucial for elastic scattering at low DM masses or large momentum transfers, and for inelastic upscattering, where additional kinetic energy is needed to overcome the mass splitting. In practice, however, phenomenological studies typically rely either on the Standard Halo Model (SHM) or, when an enhanced high-velocity tail contributes to the scattering rate, on the single simulation that includes a large Magellanic Cloud (LMC) analogue, Au-25, whose debris reaches ~ 950\kms. In this work, we instead build on a previously presented empirically-motivated reconstruction method, to construct the local DM velocity distribution, using stellar kinematics from the Gaia space telescope. We combine this reconstructed Milky Way component with the best LMC analog in the FIRE-2 simulations, and find no local DM faster than ~ 900\kms. We compare the resulting distribution with the two commonly used benchmarks, the SHM and Au-25. We then study how these different velocity distributions affect the interpretation of DD searches across all operators of the non-relativistic effective field theory of DM--nucleon interactions, for both elastic and inelastic DM. As an illustrative application, we consider the high-energy event observed in the LUX-ZEPLIN extended search. Requiring the event to remain compatible with the absence of signal in the surrounding energy sidebands, we observe the inferred inelastic DM mass splitting can be shifted by up to $\sim 130$~keV depending on the assumed high-velocity tail. Higher-resolution simulations of the high-velocity DM population reaching the detector will therefore be crucial for interpreting a future signal and setting robust limits on DM interactions.

entries.title: The (missing) gamma-ray counterparts to EP events
entries.abstract: While the connection of Fast X-ray Transients (FXTs) detected by Einstein Probe (EP) with Gamma-ray Bursts (GRBs) is increasingly compelling, most lack gamma-ray counterparts, leaving their relation to GRBs unclear. We performed a systematic search for gamma-ray counterparts to the 72 transients detected by EP in its first year, using targeted searches in Fermi/GBM and Fermi/LAT data, complemented by SVOM/GRM, SVOM/ECLAIRs, Swift/BAT and Konus-Wind. For the visible events without a gamma-ray counterpart, we derived simultaneous $3σ$ flux upper limits in the 10-1000 keV and the 0.1-1 GeV band. We find that 23 events (32%) have a gamma-ray counterpart (seven sub-threshold), while 49 events (68%) have none, despite most being visible. For events with a gamma-ray counterpart, the X-ray flux over the gamma-ray $T_{\rm 90}$ is systematically higher than over the full X-ray duration, with flux ratios $1 \lesssim F_{\rm [10-1000\,keV]}/F_{\rm [0.5-4\,keV]} \lesssim 100$, suggesting that gamma-rays are preferentially detected during the brightest X-ray phases. For events without gamma-ray counterpart, the most stringent Fermi/GBM upper limits imply $E_{\rm peak} \lesssim 30$-100 keV and, for the 14 events with measured redshifts, $L_{\rm iso}\lesssim 10^{48}-9\times10^{51}$ erg/s. If classical GRB correlations hold in this regime, these lower energetics imply lower bulk Lorentz factors ($Γ_0 \lesssim 100$), as confirmed in a few cases by afterglow constraints. No significant GeV emission was detected by Fermi/LAT, yielding $1 \lesssim F_{0.1-1\,{\rm GeV}}/F_{0.5-4\,{\rm keV}} \lesssim 10$, placing the first constraints on a potential synchrotron self-Compton component for this new population. Although individual origins remain uncertain, many EP FXTs could be compatible with the GRB population, extending it toward lower $E_{\rm peak}$, luminosities, and bulk Lorentz factors.

entries.title: Discovery of a Broad-Line Active Galactic Nucleus at $z = 9.98$
entries.abstract: The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) has uncovered a previously unexplored population of faint active galactic nuclei (AGNs) in the early Universe. We present MoM-BL-z10 at $z=9.9837\pm0.0009$, identified through a systematic search for broad-line AGNs at $z\geq6$ using public JWST/NIRSpec PRISM spectra from the DAWN JWST Archive. The PRISM spectrum exhibits a broad component in H$β$ at 5.35 microns. A narrow+broad Gaussian fit yields a broad H$β$ detection at S/N = 3.87, with FWHM = $3480^{+2040}_{-950}$ km s$^{-1}$ and $L_{{\rm H}β,{\rm broad}}=1.25^{+0.33}_{-0.31}\times10^{42}$ erg s$^{-1}$. The detection of [Ne III] $\lambda3870$ and the high [Ne III]/[O II] and [O III]/H$β$ ratios further support the AGN interpretation. Its rest-frame UV and optical continuum slopes, compact NIRCam morphology, and a tentative MIRI F770W detection suggest similarities to Little Red Dots (LRDs). The broad H$β$ detection enables the first virial SMBH mass estimate at $z\sim10$. We derive $M_{\rm BH}=3.6^{+5.8}_{-1.7}\times10^7 M_\odot$ and $λ_{\rm Edd}=0.11^{+0.10}_{-0.07}$ using the standard single-epoch virial calibration and quasar bolometric correction. We also consider an alternative scenario adopting the LRD-specific bolometric correction and assuming $λ_{\rm Edd}=1$, which yields $M_{\rm BH}=2.1^{+0.6}_{-0.5}\times10^6 M_\odot$. Under either scenario, the inferred SMBH mass at a cosmic age of only 470 Myr highlights the challenge of rapid BH growth in the early Universe, suggesting super-Eddington accretion from a stellar-mass seed or a more massive seed. As the highest-redshift broad-line AGN identified to date, MoM-BL-z10 provides a new observational benchmark for understanding the early growth of supermassive black holes.

entries.title: Saturation Level of the Streaming Instability
entries.abstract: In proto-planetary disks, gas turbulence can cluster dust grains and catalyze the formation of planetesimals. This process depends on the strength of the turbulence. Here, we evaluate the turbulence strength that is induced by the streaming instability. Based on the amount of free energy available, we estimate the viscous parameter to be alpha ~ St Pi^2 f(epsilon), where St (< 1) is the Stokes number of the streaming grains, Pi is the dimensionless pressure gradient, and f (epsilon) is an explicit function of epsilon, the local dust-to-gas density ratio. This estimate explains the results of many previous studies, and is also supported by our additional tailor-made simulations. We discuss two easy applications of our result, one is a self-consistent dust scale height, one is the astrophysical relevance of a pressure bump. Lastly, while this work allows one to characterize the streaming turbulence, we emphasize our current inability to connect the strength of turbulence to the formation of planetesimals.

entries.title: A combined HST and JWST analysis of the stellar population in Draco II
entries.abstract: Draco II (Dra II) is one of the faintest and most metal-poor Milky Way satellites known, yet its nature as either an ultra-faint dwarf galaxy or an extended globular cluster remains debated. We perform a photometric analysis of the stellar population of Dra II reducing deep multi-band observations from the Hubble Space Telescope (HST) and the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST). We select Dra II member stars based on their proper motions and photometric quality criteria. For the first time, optical and infrared photometry are combined to produce a stellar catalogue reaching 50 percent completeness at $F814W = 26.5$ mag (corresponding to the absolute magnitude $M_{F814W} = 10.1$ mag). The colour-magnitude diagram confirms that Dra II hosts an old stellar population with an age of $13.5_{-1.5}^{+1.7}$ Gyr at a distance of $19.2\pm0.9$ kpc. We measure an $α$-enhanced stellar population with a low mean metallicity of $[\rm Fe/H]_{CaHK} = -2.38 \pm 0.17$ dex and confirm the presence of an intrinsic metallicity spread of $σ_{[\rm Fe/H]} = 0.85 \pm 0.13$ dex. We identify 10 unresolved main-sequence binary stars in the HST catalogue with mass ratios $q > 0.5$ in the mass range $0.43<M_1/M_\odot<0.71$, corresponding to a binary fraction of $f_{bin}^{q>0.5} = 0.21 \pm 0.07$. This value is higher than those typically observed in globular clusters and lies near the upper range measured in open clusters. The stellar mass function is best modelled by a single power law with a slope of $1.53\pm0.26$ over the mass range $0.13$--$0.77\ M_\odot$. We find no evidence of mass segregation. Consistent results are obtained independently from the JWST catalogue. Combining these findings strongly suggests that Draco II is best classified as an ultra-faint dwarf galaxy rather than a globular cluster.

entries.title: Prior volume effect inflates the gravitational-wave background in pulsar timing arrays
entries.abstract: Pulsar timing arrays (PTAs) have found evidence for a nanohertz gravitational-wave background (GWB) whose amplitude exceeds most predictions based on supermassive black hole binaries (SMBHBs). Using NANOGrav 15-year data, we show that a substantial part of this excess arises from a prior volume effect. The GWB amplitude is constrained mainly by the pulsars' auto-correlations, where the GWB is degenerate with each pulsar's intrinsic red noise. By decomposing the GWB posterior, we find that marginalizing over the standard log-uniform red-noise priors introduces a prior volume term that favors a stronger GWB, pulling the inferred amplitude more than $2σ$ above the maximum-likelihood estimate. The Hellings-Downs (HD) cross-correlations, which measure the GWB alone, are not strong enough to counter the volume term. The profile likelihood, a cross-correlation-only estimator, and priors that are uniform in power or informed by the pulsar population all avoid or reduce this effect and lower the amplitude into agreement with SMBHBs. The revised priors also yield a steeper GWB spectrum closer to the SMBHB predictions, strengthen the evidence for HD correlations, and weaken the preference for new-physics sources over SMBHBs.

entries.title: A Hybrid Neural Network Emulator for M1 Neutrino Reaction Rates in Binary Neutron Star Merger Simulations
entries.abstract: We present a neural network emulator for the bns_nurates library, which computes neutrino reaction rates used in binary neutron star merger simulations. Following a hybrid strategy, we emulate only the computationally dominant two-dimensional reactions---pair processes, bremsstrahlung, and inelastic neutrino-electron scattering---while evaluating the inexpensive one-dimensional processes still with bns_nurates. We find that the emulator reproduces the opacities to within a few percent across the relevant thermodynamic conditions and accelerates their evaluation by roughly an order of magnitude. When deployed in a global Athenak binary neutron star merger simulation, it recovers the remnant structure, neutrino luminosities, and ejecta composition of a reference run using the full bns_nurates library, at approximately half the overall cost

entries.title: Exploring PSR J0901-4046 as an ultra-slowly rotating neutron star versus a white dwarf
entries.abstract: The source PSR J0901-4046 shows a very long rotational period, of $\approx 75.88$ s. In fact, its long period suggests that it could be a white dwarf. We examine the properties of the source and compare the outcomes under the hypotheses of the source being a highly magnetized white dwarf (B-WD) and neutron star. We find that assuming it to be a B-WD with a surface field $\sim 10^{10}$ G explains many properties, including its storage/rotational energy, explaining luminosity. On the contrary, the neutron star-based idea, particularly if examined under the conventional spin down mechanism, requires an unusually high surface magnetic field $\gtrsim 10^{14}$ G, even exceeding $10^{16}$ G, depending on the obliquity angle and emission mechanism. The source also sits very close to AR Sco, a white dwarf pulsar, in the period and period-derivative plane. We suggest that the source is a B-WD. Along with AR Sco, it being a B-WD constrains the death line model. B-WD hypothesis alleviates the necessity of an unusually high magnetic field hindering pair production for PSR J0901-4046 under the neutron star hypothesis. We argue that some rotation-powered pulsars with extreme properties may possibly be white dwarfs rather than neutron stars.

entries.title: Unveiling the correlation between the UV 2175 Å dust attenuation bump, PAH emission, and gas-phase metallicity at cosmic noon
entries.abstract: The UV 2175 Å attenuation bump is one of the most prominent yet poorly understood features of galaxy attenuation curves. Its main candidate carrier is polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) molecules, which are more prevalent in high-metallicity environments. We present the first systematic study of the relationship between PAH abundance and the UV bump in 49 galaxies at cosmic noon (1.5 < z < 2.7), examining its dependence on stellar mass, star formation rate (SFR), and V-band optical depth. For 19 galaxies, we also investigate gas-phase metallicity using oxygen abundances. We measure the bump amplitude from VLT/MUSE spectroscopy and derive galaxy properties, including the PAH-to-dust mass fraction $q_{\rm PAH}$, through spectral energy distribution fitting with Prospector, combining JWST/NIRCam and JWST/MIRI photometry. Oxygen abundances are derived from strong-line diagnostics using Keck/MOSFIRE and JWST/NIRSpec data. We find a positive correlation between bump amplitude $E_{\rm bump}$ and $q_{\rm PAH}$ (Spearman $ρ= 0.60$). UV bumps are rarely detected at low $q_{\rm PAH}$, supporting PAHs as their primary carriers. Both $E_{\rm bump}$ and $q_{\rm PAH}$ correlate with stellar mass, oxygen abundance, and optical depth, and anticorrelate with specific SFR, suggesting that PAHs and the UV bump are suppressed in low-metallicity, dust-poor, and/or intensely star-forming environments. This is consistent with PAH destruction in environments with limited dust shielding and/or strong radiation fields. A principal component analysis of $E_{\rm bump}$, $q_{\rm PAH}$, optical depth, specific SFR, and oxygen abundance explains 97% of the variance, suggesting that previously reported correlations with stellar mass reflect an underlying dependence on metallicity. Finally, variations in dust geometry may explain the wide range of bump amplitudes (0-0.5 mag) at high $q_{\rm PAH}$.

entries.title: The renormalization-group running of neutrino mixing is undetectable
entries.abstract: Quantum corrections make the parameters of a theory depend on an arbitrary renormalization scale, $μ$. The renormalization-group (RG) running of neutrino masses and mixing is a standard tool to relate models defined at a high mass scale to measured values. A growing body of work holds that the running is also directly observable: a neutrino produced or detected at momentum transfer $Q$ would carry the mixing matrix evaluated at $μ= Q$. Proposed signatures include flavor change at zero distance from the source, shifts in the measured CP-violation phase, and an anomalous flavor composition of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos. We show that this premise is incorrect. The mixing is a property of the neutrino itself, fixed by its self-energy on the mass shell, not by the process that produces or detects it. Setting $μ= Q$ is legitimate, but then large logarithms in the self-energy undo the running; the premise incorrectly drops them. Hence, apart from small vertex and box corrections, every experiment measures the same mixing: the running is undetectable. We illustrate this in the Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model, two seesaw models, and the Standard Model effective field theory. Independently, short-baseline data already limit the change of any one mixing angle between pion decay and detection at $Q$ of a few GeV to below $0.7^\circ$--$2.4^\circ$.

entries.title: Ammonia Fitting of Multiple Velocity Components in High-Mass Star-Forming Regions
entries.abstract: We perform a multiple velocity component analysis of ammonia (NH$_3$) gas from KEYSTONE, a Green Bank Telescope survey covering 11 giant molecular clouds (GMCs) at distances from 0.7 to 2.7 kpc. We extend existing codes to enable simultaneous fitting of up to three velocity components in NH$_3$ (1,1) with radiative transfer. Using our multiple component fitting technique, we produce the best maps of the centroid velocity and velocity dispersion in these clouds to date. Over the entire survey, multiple velocity components were seen in 13% of pixels where we detect and fit NH$_3$ emission, primarily in clusters at the heart of the GMCs. In these multiple component pixels, the median measured NH$_3$ linewidth decreased by a factor of 1.4 compared to equivalent single-component measurements, but there are also significant cloud-to-cloud variations. Regions with multiple velocity components tend to be found in the densest zones of the GMCs and at the sites of high-mass star formation, indicative of multiple filaments, cores, or complex velocities associated with the formation of massive stars. Disentangling these velocity features will allow future quantitative analysis of coherent motions, such as infall and outflow, in these complex environments. The multi-component data products are available on the CADC.

entries.title: A new view of the cosmic-ray knee after LHAASO
entries.abstract: Recent LHAASO measurements offer a new view of the cosmic-ray knee by combining the all-particle spectrum and mean logarithmic mass with proton and light-component spectra across the PeV region. This contribution reviews these results and their implications for Galactic acceleration and transport. Approximately charge-ordered proton and helium knees coexist with different spectral evolution, while their turnover shapes constrain source populations and escape mechanisms. These measurements anchor an elemental ``ladder'' that, extended to heavier nuclei, will be crucial for establishing how far the Galactic component persists and where the Galactic--extragalactic transition takes place.

entries.title: Link between the properties of circumgalactic outflows and the recent star formation history of their host galaxies
entries.abstract: Galactic outflows play a key role in galaxy evolution, yet their connection to the star formation history of their host galaxies remains poorly constrained. Building on previous work modeling extended Mg II emission of galaxies observed with VLT/MUSE to infer outflow properties, we investigate how these properties depend on the recent SFH. We derive non-parametric SFHs by fitting spectroscopic and photometric data with linear combinations of single stellar population models, and compute star formation rates over different timescales sensitive to recent stochastic bursts. We find moderate correlations between these SFRs (and sSFRs) and the kinematic properties of the outflows, namely maximum velocity and radial acceleration rate. Such correlations are not recovered using SFR tracers based on [O II] luminosity or parametric SFHs, highlighting the importance of capturing bursty star formation on timescales consistent with the traveling time of ejected gas into the circumgalactic medium. Using the extent and kinematics of the Mg II halos, we estimate each galaxy's outflow launching time and compute the SFR averaged over the relevant timescale. We identify a correlation between this SFR and the maximum outflow velocity, although it is not significantly stronger than those obtained using fixed averaging timescales. This suggests that the properties of Mg II halos are shaped by a series of star formation events rather than by a single dominant burst. Lastly, we find faster outflows in galaxies whose recent star formation is dominated by one or a few concentrated episodes, whereas galaxies with star formation spread more evenly over time exhibit slower outflows. These results indicate that the circumgalactic medium acts as a dynamical archive of recent star formation, linking bursty galaxy growth to outflow kinematics and providing a direct observational constraint on feedback models.

entries.title: The MIni-Halos in MIni-Clusters (MIMIC) project: New insights into the origin of mini-halos from a LOFAR, uGMRT, and MeerKAT study of diffuse radio emission in Abell 496 and ZwCl 235
entries.abstract: We aim at investigating the presence of diffuse radio emission in low-mass (M$_{500}\leq3\times10^{14}$ M$_{\odot}$), relaxed galaxy clusters. We present a pilot study for the MIMIC (MIni-halos in MIni-Clusters) project, focusing on Abell 496 and ZwCl 235, using LOFAR (54, 144 MHz), uGMRT (400, 650 MHz), and MeerKAT (1.28 GHz) data, as well as Chandra X-ray data. We detect diffuse radio emission in the central 100 kpc of both Abell 496 and ZwCl 235, spatially confined within sloshing-induced cold fronts seen in X-ray images. The diffuse sources satisfy the classification criteria for radio mini-halos and represent the least powerful known to date, with 1.4 GHz radio powers of $(2.2\pm0.2)\times10^{22}$ W/Hz in Abell 496 and $(1.3\pm0.3)\times10^{22}$ W/Hz in ZwCl 235. The mini-halos have steep spectra ($-1.9\leqα\leq-1.4$), and in Abell 496 we find outward steepening of the spectral index. In both clusters, the radio and X-ray surface brightness are correlated over the diffuse source extent, with sub-linear or nearly linear slopes depending on frequency. Separately, we present the properties of two extended (>200 kpc) tailed radio galaxies in both clusters. The steep spectra, sub-linear radio-X-ray correlations, and confinement within cold fronts suggest that contribution from fossil plasma advected from the central radio galaxy and plausible turbulent re-acceleration are at play in Abell 496 and ZwCl 235. These two systems allow us to extend mini-halo scaling relations toward the low-power regime. We confirm a strong correlation between the mini-halo radio power and the cool core X-ray luminosity, with $P_{1.4} \propto L_{X,70}^{1.5\pm0.2}$. We find, for the first time, tentative indications that mini-halos with steeper radio spectra may preferentially be associated with lower core X-ray luminosities and lower radio power. (abridged)

entries.title: PIANISTpy: A JAX-based Python package for velocity-anisotropic astrophysical equilibrium models
entries.abstract: The hierarchical assembly of dark matter haloes and galaxies via mergers and anisotropic mass accretion naturally imprints non-trivial velocity anisotropy onto haloes and galaxies, an empirical fact emerging from cosmological simulations. However, dynamical studies based on idealised numerical simulations typically assume isotropic velocity distributions for the systems studied. This is mainly because no tools exist to construct anisotropic initial conditions with fully self-consistent (i.e., physical and instability-free) truncation boundary conditions for finite spatial extents. Here we present the first such analytical framework that performs truncation in phase space, with two distinct approaches to guarantee either the monotonicity of output distribution functions or identical truncated density profiles. We additionally present the open-source JAX-based GPU-accelerated Python package PIANISTpy (Particle Initial conditions with ANISoTropy) for constructing spherical, non-rotating initial conditions, supporting arbitrary double-power-law analytical radial density profiles and a library of analytical anisotropy profiles. This framework further permits the construction of systems with non-analytical anisotropy profiles via an arbitrary linear superposition of all implemented analytical anisotropy models as basis functions. PIANISTpy also outputs 3D velocity profiles and line-of-sight-integrated observables with end-to-end differentiability for rapid gradient-based Monte Carlo inference, and self-consistent local dark matter velocity distributions of anisotropic haloes beyond the unphysical Maxwell-Boltzmann simplification adopted in terrestrial detection experiments. We discuss use cases and demonstrate PIANISTpy's orders-of-magnitude higher numerical solver accuracy and superior dynamical stability of particle initial conditions relative to existing tools, including galpy and AGAMA.

entries.title: Constraints on Reionization from Planck Low-$\ell$ EE Polarization and the Lyman-Series Forests
entries.abstract: CMB measurements tightly constrain the Thomson scattering optical depth ($τ_{\rm es}$), but they still permit a broad range of degenerate reionization histories. Incorporating Lyman-series forest constraints on the end of reionization can alleviate the degeneracy and narrow the range of allowed histories. We explore this effect using forest measurements combined with full Planck likelihoods. We apply upper limits on the neutral fraction at $4.9\lesssim z\lesssim6.9$ derived from the dark pixel fraction, as well as a lower limit at $z=5.8$ from damping-wing-like features on the edges of long dark gaps in stacked forest spectra. We find that neither the choice of parametric vs. non-parametric reionization model, nor the choice among different forest data combinations, produces a significant shift in $τ_{\rm es}$ or the other cosmological parameters. Instead, forest constraints primarily redistribute $τ_{\rm es}$ in redshift. Combining dark pixel, damping-wing-like, and CMB measurements, we find $z_{50}=7.7^{+0.7}_{-0.8}$ and a 95\% upper limit of $Δz_{90}<11.4$ for the midpoint and duration of reionization, respectively. The asymmetry of the reionization history ($A_z$) is not well constrained by these data. Stronger constraints can be obtained using Ly$α$ forest measurements of the mean IGM photoionization rate, at the cost of requiring more detailed modeling. Using a new semi-analytic reionization model, we obtain (model-dependent) constraints of $z_{50} = 7.4^{+0.2}_{-0.3}$, $Δz_{90}=6.0^{+0.8}_{-1.0}$, and $A_z = 2.4^{+0.3}_{-0.7}$. We also find evidence that the ionizing emissivity of reionization sources declines after $z=7-8$, perhaps signaling a decline in the escape fraction and/or the onset of a feedback process. Our results motivate the development of forest likelihood products and fast forward models for its transmission statistics.

entries.title: Can we constrain the binary neutron star merger time from kilonova light curves?
entries.abstract: The joint observation of gravitational waves (GWs) from a binary neutron star (BNS) merger (GW170817), together with a short Gamma-Ray Burst (GRB 170817A) and a kilonova (KN, AT2017gfo), marked the birth of multimessenger astronomy with GWs, and demonstrated the informative power of multimessenger observations. More BNS merger and KN detections are expected , thanks to the increasing sensitivity of GW detectors and the advent of new electromagnetic facilities such as the Vera C. Rubin Observatory. However, the association between a BNS merger and a KN might not be trivial: the detection of a KN might not coincide with the onset of the EM emission, making it difficult to define a temporal window to assess the coincidence with a GW event. In this work we investigate the possibility to constrain the BNS merger time from KN light curves, exploring different observing conditions and with focus on the Vera C. Rubin Observatory. We used different KN models and different inference frameworks to simulate and fit KN light curves. We explored different cadences and wavelength coverages for observations, to investigate how the different observing conditions can affect the capability to recover the BNS merger time. The tests performed also include real data related to AT2017gfo, plus a few GRBs that have been associated to possible KN candidates. We find that, under realistic observing conditions with the Vera C. Rubin Observatory, the BNS merger time can be recovered with a precision of 5.5 days (90\% CI) with a best-case scenario with an accuracy of 0.18 day and a precision of 0.74 day (90 \% CI). Results can slightly improve (by $\sim$ 5 \%) if the source redshift is available. Upper limits near the merger time can also improve the results, reducing the width of the posterior by $\sim60$ \%. The BNS merger time estimate could also benefit from EM follow-up observations with other telescopes.

entries.title: A Comprehensive X-ray Characterization of the Pulsar Wind Nebula CTB 87: Evidence for Reverse-Shock Interaction from Its X-ray and Broadband Emissions
entries.abstract: We present a comprehensive X-ray study of the pulsar wind nebula (PWN) CTB 87, utilizing new NuSTAR observations and archival Chandra and XMM-Newton data. Our joint analysis reveals that the PWN's X-ray spectrum exhibits significant curvature, well described by a broken or cutoff power law. The broken power-law fit yields photon indices $Γ_{1}=1.89\pm 0.05$ and $Γ_{2}=2.73 \pm 0.10$ below and above a break energy of $E_{\rm b}=5.12 \pm 0.26$ keV, respectively, while the cutoff power-law fit gives $Γ=1.23 \pm 0.10$ and $E_{\rm c} = 5.29 \pm 0.67$ keV. Spatially resolved spectroscopy confirms a previously observed radial softening of $Γ$, indicating significant synchrotron cooling as electrons move outward from the pulsar. We employed leptonic emission scenarios to model the broadband emission from CTB 87, focusing on the measured X-ray spectrum and the radial profiles. While an evolutionary one-zone model can explain the general features of the broadband spectral energy distribution (SED), its predictions do not fully reproduce the observed X-ray spectrum. Our multi-zone modeling demonstrates that the hard electron distribution required to explain the X-ray spectrum cannot account for the observed gamma-ray SED. This discrepancy suggests the presence of an additional electron population, possibly linked to the reverse shock interaction, and highlights CTB 87 as an evolved PWN whose broadband emission cannot be captured by these simple SED models. We discuss the potential origins for this second electron population and its implications for understanding the evolution of PWNe.

entries.title: FAUST XXXII. Chemically layered structures and ionisation in the disk and envelope of NGC 1333 IRAS 4C
entries.abstract: Recent molecular line observations with high spatial resolutions have revealed vertical chemical stratification in Class I/II disks (i.e. chemical composition changing with height in the vertical direction of the disk), as well as a radial variation of ionisation rates. However, such chemical layered structures in Class 0 disk and envelope systems have been investigated only for limited objects, such as L1527. In the context of the ALMA Large Program FAUST, we report the results of molecular line observations toward the disk and envelope around the low-mass Class 0 protostar NGC 1333 IRAS 4C in the Perseus Molecular Cloud. Previous observations have shown that the disk rotation axis of this object is largely tilted to the line of sight, making it suitable for studying the molecular abundance distribution as a function of disk height. We found that the molecules known as gas density tracers such as C18O and H2CO are distributed around the disk midplane. In addition, molecules known as tracers of photochemical reactions such as CCH and c-C3H2 are distributed in the low-density upper layers of the disk, unlike the distribution in L1527. Moreover, the column density ratio of HCO+/CO derived from the H13CO+ and C18O line emission suggests that the ionisation degree and the ionisation rate vary with the disk radius and they are larger in the outer region of the disk and envelope.

entries.title: Probing the QPO and spectro-temporal evolution of MAXI J1750-327 with XPoSat during its first detected outburst : Constraints on black-hole mass and spin
entries.abstract: We present a comprehensive timing and broadband spectral study of the newly discovered black hole low-mass X-ray binary candidate MAXI J1750-327 during its August 2026 outburst, using 11 continuous observations obtained with the XSPECT instrument onboard XPoSat. During epochs 1-2, we detect prominent type C QPO exhibiting a systematic upward frequency drift, accompanied by a prominent low-frequency noise component, with a clear transition from type-C to type-B, with subsequent disappearance of QPOs after epoch 4. Broadband spectral modeling reveals that this timing transition is directly mirrored by a fundamental restructuring of the accretion geometry. The inner disk temperature abruptly increases before settling into a steady range, accompanied by a steep reduction in disk normalization across the transition from epoch 3 to 4. This behavior signifies an active dynamical inward migration of the thin accretion disk toward the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO). The Comptonized flux declines sharply after the QPO turns off, suggesting a transition from a hard to soft state, through intermediate states. We also observed that the spectro-temporal correlations provide compelling physical support for the Lense-Thirring (LT) precession framework to be the origin of the type-C QPOs. Using a Bayesian framework, we constrain the black hole mass to be $M_{\rm BH}=7.92^{+6.19}_{-3.72} M_{\odot}$ and the dimensionless spin parameter to be $a_*=0.163^{+0.116}_{-0.056}$ by jointly modeling the observed type-C QPO frequencies with the global LT precession model and marginalizing over the uncertainties in distance, inclination, and diskbb normalization.

entries.title: Not so Fast: Revised Calibration of SIDM Core Collapse
entries.abstract: Self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) haloes undergo gravothermal evolution whose late-time behaviour is central to predictions for dense substructure and black-hole seed formation. We revisit the calibration of this evolution using a new spherical Direct Simulation Monte Carlo code, SphDSMC, which follows spherically symmetric SIDM systems without force softening and to substantially higher central densities than standard N-body simulations. We compare SphDSMC calculations with conventional N-body simulations and with one-dimensional gravothermal fluid models. We show that N-body results converge to SphDSMC only for softening lengths significantly smaller than those normally adopted for collisionless simulations, and that allowing multiple scatterings per particle per time step does not introduce significant errors when implemented appropriately. Calibrating the gravothermal fluid equations against SphDSMC, we find that the commonly used harmonic interpolation between the long- and short-mean-free-path conductivities is inaccurate. A gentler transition, however, yields excellent agreement for NFW haloes over a range of concentrations and truncation radii, with a single long-mean-free-path conductivity parameter. The revised calibration gives a long-mean-free-path collapse time that is somewhat shorter than previous estimates, but we show that collapse slows dramatically once the core becomes optically thick. We provide fitting functions for the late-time evolution and argue that black-hole seed formation by SIDM gravothermal collapse has generally been underestimated in duration, making it unlikely to explain the massive high-redshift black holes inferred from JWST observations without additional physics.

entries.title: White dwarf pollution in wide binaries I: the effects of stellar evolution
entries.abstract: Context. Atmospheric pollution in white dwarfs is interpreted as evidence for the accretion of rocky material from remnant planetary systems. Wide binary companions can influence the delivery of planetary material onto white dwarfs, making it essential to understand the interplay between stellar evolution and binary perturbations. Aims. We investigate how uncertainties in stellar mass-loss histories affect the dynamical evolution of remnant planetary systems in wide binaries, and assess their relative importance compared with binary perturbations in driving the accretion of rocky material onto white dwarfs. Methods. We perform REBOUND N-body simulations incorporating time-dependent stellar parameters interpolated from MESA evolutionary tracks and tidal interactions, following the dynamical evolution up to the white dwarf stage. We explore two stellar-evolution models with distinct mass-loss histories for wide binary systems hosting a Jupiter-mass planet and a planetesimal disc, spanning a range of binary architectures. Results. The adopted stellar-evolution model has only a minor effect on the survival of the planet, mainly affecting the timing and efficiency of planetesimal delivery during the white dwarf stage. Instead, the architecture of the binary primarily controls the pollution outcome: wider binaries produce the highest rates of accretion onto the white dwarf, consistent with the observed prevalence of polluted white dwarfs in wide binaries. Moreover, planetesimal reservoirs remain long-lived, with survival times increasing with binary separation, enabling Gyr-long metal pollution. Conclusions. Our results suggest that the architecture of wide binaries, rather than uncertainties in stellar evolution, is the dominant factor controlling the dynamical delivery of rocky material onto white dwarfs.

entries.title: KROME-X: a GPU-ready library for chemistry and microphysics in astrophysical simulations
entries.abstract: KROME is a Python pre-processor that writes a complete Fortran solver of chemistry and microphysics for each chemical network, widely used in astrophysical simulations. We introduce here KROME-X, a complete rewrite of KROME in modern C++, which incorporates updated physics. A code generator translates a declarative network description into a compact core (rates, right-hand side, analytic Jacobian, thermal terms, and tables), which a fixed, header-only runtime integrates with a C++ port of the `backward differentiation formula' method of CVODE (SUNDIALS). The physics is validated against legacy KROME and independent references. On the legacy test cases KROME-X reproduces legacy KROME to the accuracy of the solvers, wherever the physics is the same, and is up to 13.5 times faster at equal tolerance. On NVIDIA A100 GPUs, it can outperform its share of a computing node from a few thousand cells per call, with the highest throughput (5 to 30) obtained for $10^5$ cells per batch. Networks of hundreds of species still run faster on the CPU due to the GPU's limited memory capacity. The new version also includes, among other changes, on-the-fly co-evolution of a photon field alongside chemistry, which conserves photons exactly; the secondary ionizations using the photoelectron energy of each absorption; dust evolution in size and temperature with a true grain energy equation; line cooling rates rebuilt from current atomic and molecular data, and incorporating optical thickness effects. KROME-X therefore represents the natural successor of KROME and provides a portable, extensible framework for astrochemical kinetics on both CPUs and GPUs for future hydrodynamic simulations.

entries.title: X-ray Comptonization in an Accreting Kerr Black Hole System with a Tilted Disc and Thermal Corona: A General-Relativistic Monte Carlo Simulation. II. Polarization Signatures
entries.abstract: Relativistic precession of the inner accretion flow is widely invoked to explain low-frequency QPOs, and the Relativistic Precession Model (RPM) predicts phase-dependent X-ray polarization. However, IXPE observations challenge simple precession and Comptonization models; for example: SwiftJ1727.8-1613 shows weak or undetected QPO-phase polarization modulation, while IGRJ17091-3624 shows a hard-state polarization degree (DOP) of ~9%, versus ~4% in other hard-state black hole binaries. In Paper I, we presented a general-relativistic Monte Carlo (GRMC) model of X-ray reprocessing in a misaligned, warped two-zone disc around a Kerr black hole with a hot, optically thin corona. We computed energy spectra, photon path-length and arrival-time distributions, and X-ray lags. Here, we extend the model to track photon polarization using Walker-Penrose parallel transport and polarized Compton and disc scattering. We calculate the energy-resolved degree and angle of polarization and their precession-phase modulation versus coronal optical depth, outer-disc albedo, photon-injection radius, and observer inclination. We find that gravitational light bending raises the mean DOP and enhances modulation, whereas coronal scattering and reflection from the misaligned outer disc lower the DOP and suppress modulation. The steady outer-disc polarization further dilutes the inner-flow signal. Their competition can produce weak, nearly unmodulated polarization or a high, strongly modulated signal. Strong scattering and reflection can explain SwiftJ1727.8-1613's weak modulation, while strong light bending and weak secondary scattering can explain IGRJ17091-3624's high DOP. Our results provide a framework for interpreting unusual X-ray polarization and testable predictions for constraining black hole parameters, coronal properties, and disc-warp geometry with IXPE, XPoSat, and eXTP.

entries.title: Interpreting the $γ$-ray emission from Westerlund 1: hadronic or leptonic?
entries.abstract: High-energy $γ$-ray emission has been detected from several star clusters, indicating that these sources are sites of cosmic-ray acceleration. However, it is still unclear whether the $γ$-ray emission is of hadronic or leptonic origin. We present a comprehensive study of the $γ$-ray emission from Westerlund 1, under the assumption that high-energy particles are accelerated at the cluster WTS. We investigate both the hadronic and leptonic scenarios by fitting simultaneously the spectrum and morphology of the $γ$-ray emission. We numerically solve the transport equations for non-thermal protons and electrons for a given $K_\rm{ep}$ and derive their energy and spatial distributions. $γ$ rays are produced either by hadronic pp interactions of protons with the target gas or by inverse Compton scattering of relativistic electrons (both primary and secondary) with the ambient photon fields. We also calculate the synchrotron emission from these electrons. The predicted SEDs are compared with the $γ$-ray measurements by Fermi-LAT and HESS and with the X-ray upper limit derived by eROSITA. For reasonable model parameters, we find that in the case of Bohm diffusion, both the leptonic and hadronic scenarios can account for the observed multi-wavelength spectrum and $γ$-ray morphology. However, in the case of Kraichnan diffusion, better motivated in star clusters, only the hadronic scenario can explain the observations, while the leptonic scenario fails to reproduce the highest-energy $γ$-ray data points. For the leptonic scenario, the magnetic field immediately downstream of the shock can be constrained to be $\lesssim$ a few $μ$G thanks to the eROSITA upper limit. On the other hand, in order to explain the $γ$-ray observations with hadronic emission alone, the gas density inside the bubble should be $\gtrsim 1.2 \, \rm{cm}^{-3}$.

entries.title: Direct Injection of Chemically-Enhanced Plasma into a Solar Flare Arcade
entries.abstract: The magnetic reconnection event that drives "standard" solar flares ejects material from the reconnection site, loading mass directly onto the newly-reconnected flare arcade. To et al (2024) suggested that this model can explain observations of the distribution of elemental abundances measured in post-flare loops: the reconnection exhaust directly injects plasma with coronal abundances onto the arcade, flowing from the apex downwards. We test this idea directly by modeling the spatiotemporal variation of elements with low first ionization potential (FIP), and directly inject material near loop apices. We show that this direct injection is capable of producing enhancements similar in magnitude and spatial spread across the corona to those observed during the gradual phase of an X11.9 flare. We also show that direct chromospheric heating strongly limits the width of the low-FIP enhancement to a narrow region near the injection site. The enhancement of low-FIP elemental abundances naturally explains bright knots commonly observed near the top of flare arcades.

entries.title: The H IX galaxy survey IV: What does the molecular gas reveal in HI eXtreme galaxies
entries.abstract: Galaxies with extreme amounts of neutral atomic hydrogen (HI), known as HI-eXtreme (HIX) galaxies, paradoxically exhibit normal or low star formation rates. To investigate the bottleneck in their star formation, we present ALMA CO(1-0) observations for five HIX survey galaxies: ESO208-G026, ESO378-G003, ESO381-G005, ESO417-G018, and ESO055-G013. While these systems possess massive, extended HI discs, their molecular gas discs are compact with normal H$_{2}$ masses relative to their stellar mass. Dynamical modelling with 3DBarolo reveals that the HI and molecular gas are kinematically consistent. Both gas phases show high velocity dispersions, indicating enhanced turbulence compared to regular late-type galaxies. We calculate the specific angular momentum for the stellar, atomic, and molecular components alongside the global stability parameter ($q$). Most of the system angular momentum is stored in the HI discs, rendering them globally stable against collapse. This stability suppresses the atomic-to-molecular gas conversion, as evidenced by extremely long HI depletion times contrasted with typical H$_{2}$ depletion times. The high angular momentum and HI excess likely originate from past gas accretion or recent tidal interactions; this is especially apparent in ESO378-G003 and ESO381-G005, which exhibit extended HI structures and positive tidal indices.

entries.title: Rotation in the Lagoon Nebula with K2
entries.abstract: A low-mass star's rotation rate drives its magnetic field, and in the case of young stars, also affects accretion and planetary formation. Observations of the rotation rates of young stars help constrain models of star and planet formation. We present rotation rates from K2 observations of stars in the ~1-2 Myr Lagoon Nebula, one of the youngest clusters with space-based rotation rates available. From 414 light curves we obtain reliable rotation periods for 325 stars; 124 of them are disk-bearing and 201 are disk-free. This constitutes a significant increase in the collection of K2 rotation rates available for ~1-5 Myr stars. The overall distribution is broadly consistent with expectations, in that the slowest rotators are mid-K and both lower and higher masses are on average faster rotating. There is weak evidence that disked stars rotate more slowly. There are a few complex periodic variables, but they appear to be surprisingly high mass compared to prior known examples of this kind of object.

entries.title: The MAGE Project: Size Evolution and Disk Formation in Massive Galaxies at Cosmic Dawn
entries.abstract: We investigate size evolution and disk formation with a new suite of eleven cosmological zoom-in simulations, Massive Assembly of Galaxies in the Early universe (MAGE), run with RAMSES at $\sim10\,\mathrm{pc}$ resolution until $z\simeq9$. The target galaxies span stellar masses of $M_\star\simeq2\times10^8$-$3\times10^{10}\,M_\odot$ at $z=9$. The stellar half-mass radius grows steeply with stellar mass at low masses, turns over near $M_\star\simeq5\times10^9\,M_\odot$, and evolves weakly with redshift. The intrinsic UV sizes in MAGE overlap the compact end of observed distributions, including the compact strong-line systems, but not the more extended population at $z>9$. Dust, PSF-limited size measurements, and our overdense environments may contribute to this offset. In the simulations, stars dominate the mass within the half-mass radius above $M_\star\simeq5\times10^8\,M_\odot$, where the central circular speed exceeds a characteristic stellar-feedback scale. Outflows are then increasingly retained within the galaxy, consistent with gas recycling on galactic rather than halo scales, which sustains central gas supply and drives a compaction-like central buildup. The turnover in size at $M_\star\simeq5\times10^9\,M_\odot$ coincides with rapid growth of rotational support to $v/σ\simeq1.5$-$3$ in star-forming gas and stars younger than 10Myr, as the central circular speed exceeds the halo virial speed, which the star-forming gas velocity dispersion tracks. The subsequent low central gas fraction, declining central star formation, and younger outskirts suggest the onset of inside-out quenching.

entries.title: Investigating a TeV-Halo Candidate around PSR J1928+1746 with HAWC
entries.abstract: We present an updated High-Altitude Water Cherenkov (HAWC) analysis of the crowded Galactic-plane area near PSR J1928+1746, which was previously linked to the extended source 3HWC J1928+178. With 2904 days of HAWC data, improved event reconstruction, and a multicomponent likelihood model that includes six TeV source components and Galactic diffuse emission, we describe the region using six components and find a distinct, moderately extended source close to PSR J1928+1746. This source, HAWC J1928+1750, is detected from about 2 TeV to above 100 TeV and is well-described by a log-parabola spectrum with normalization $K = 5.0 \times 10^{-15}$ TeV$^{-1}$ cm$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$ at 12 TeV, index $α= 2.09$, curvature $β= 0.35$, and Gaussian extension $σ= 0.19^\circ$. Interpreting the emission using diffusion-halo templates under the assumption $B = 8 μ\mathrm{G}$ yields the diffusion coefficient D(100 TeV) = $2.1 \times 10^{27}$ cm$^2$ s$^{-1}$, which is about 500 times smaller than typical interstellar diffusion values at similar energies. This suggests that particle transport around PSR J1928+1746 is strongly suppressed under the TeV-halo interpretation. The TeV spectrum is consistent with leptonic inverse-Compton emission originating from pulsar-injected electrons and positrons, which requires less than approximately 1% of the pulsar's characteristic spin-down energy. However, a hadronic contribution from the surrounding environment cannot be excluded.

entries.title: NGC 3227 Blinks: An Extreme Changing-Look Event in a Seyfert Galaxy
entries.abstract: We report a rapid optical changing-look event in the Seyfert galaxy NGC 3227: the optical continuum faded by more than 70% and broad H-beta emission nearly disappeared within weeks, before recovering within two months. Damped random walk simulations calibrated to the source's normal variability show that such a decline is unlikely for stochastic accretion fluctuations (p = 0.002). Simultaneous Swift monitoring reveals X-ray spectral hardening, pointing to enhanced line-of-sight absorption. During the dim state, reverberation mapping yields a persistent 6-8 day lag between the continuum and broad H-beta, showing that the broad-line region continued to reverberate and placing the obscurer interior to the broad-line region. Photoionization calculations require a fully ionized, Compton-thick column with N_H ~ 1.5 x 10^24 cm^-2 to reproduce the optical continuum suppression. Together, these observations demonstrate that compact, high-column-density obscurers interior to the broad-line region can produce extreme optical changing-look behavior on week timescales.

entries.title: Unveiling Accretion-Disk Reverberation Beneath BLR Contamination with TILDE
entries.abstract: We present a Bayesian framework, Two-stage Inference for Light curve DEcomposition (TILDE), for mapping the accretion disk and the broad line region (BLR) from active galactic nuclei (AGN) multi-band light curves. By inferring delayed BLR contamination from the underlying disk variability, TILDE provides the delay measurements of the disk as well as the BLR. We validate TILDE using synthetic data, finding that TILDE recovers the known time delays of the disk and BLR. By applying TILDE to the Seoul National University AGN Monitoring Project sample, we find that the inferred BLR light curves match the observed H$β$ emission light curves, providing consistent BLR lags compared to the reported H$β$ lags. Using the lag spectrum, effectively corrected for the BLR contamination, we find that the disk size is broadly consistent with the standard thin-disk model, suggesting that BLR contamination can significantly bias the disk size derived from the cross-correlation analysis of the broad-band photometry. These results demonstrate that the new inference method is a powerful tool for determining both disk and BLR sizes from broad-band photometry in the era of time-domain surveys.

entries.title: Double-Shock Radiation in Supernova Wind Breakout and EP260321a
entries.abstract: We study the supernova (SN) shock breakout (SBO) from an optically thick stellar wind. The SN ejecta-wind interaction forms a forward shock (FS) plus reverse shock (RS) structure. The RS's internal energy and shock velocity are both a fraction $μ\lesssim1/6$ of the FS's. The lower RS velocity makes it easier to build up local thermal equilibrium (LTE) and generate blackbody (BB) emission. In the same time a $μ^{-1}\gtrsim6$ times larger non-BB emission may be produced by the likely non-LTE FS. We apply the theory to analyze the recent detected type Ic-BL SN2026gzf associated X-ray flash EP260321a, and find it is naturally accounted for by a SN wind breakout: the $\sim0.13$\,keV, thermal SBO emission can be produced by the RS during the interaction of a typical type Ic-BL SN ejecta ($E_k\sim10^{52}$erg and $M_e\sim1M_\odot$) and a stellar wind with a mass $M_w\sim10^{-4}M_\odot$ confined within a radius $r_w\sim10^{13}$cm; the X-ray rise time is mainly determined by the RS emission time, whereas the long duration and decrease time are due to the scatterings of SBO photons by a distant shell-like medium which has a large photosphere, $r_{ph}\sim10^{14}$\,cm; the early, within 30\,ks, optical emission can be naturally explained by the cooling emission of a shocked pure C/O envelope, since the observed SBO onset is delayed by $\gtrsim$ a few ks due to the large medium photosphere. BB+non-BB components from RS and FS, respectively, may be common in SN wind breakouts. SBO observations can be crucial in the study of progenitor stars by providing information for the ejecta from the SN explosion and the nearby wind from the pre-SN activities.

entries.title: Hybrid Stars with a Crossover Equation of State
entries.abstract: The possible occurrence of a phase transition in superdense nuclear matter remains an open problem in nuclear physics. In particular, the transition from purely hadronic matter to the hypothesized deconfined quark matter is a subject of considerable interest. Beyond its fundamental significance, this transition has important implications for the physics of compact objects, including neutron stars, quark stars, and hybrid stars. The conventional approaches to this problem involve the Maxwell and Gibbs constructions, both of which have been extensively studied and applied. In the present study, we focus on a third, alternative approach based on a smooth transition from hadronic to quark matter through the so-called switching function. More specifically, the present work focuses on two main objectives. The first is to systematically investigate the influence of the symmetry energy on the transition densities and chemical potentials associated with the transition to quark matter. Subsequently, we attempt to physically constrain and parametrize the two parameters characterizing the switching function, ensuring that the transition from hadronic to quark matter is not merely continuous but also consistent with relevant physical requirements. The main conclusion is that, with an appropriate choice of the aforementioned parameters, the phenomenological model becomes more physically motivated and can serve as a useful tool for investigating the structure and properties of hybrid compact objects. Moreover, this approach offers the flexibility to predict the properties of compact objects that lie beyond the scope of standard neutron-star theory, such as objects characterized by relatively low masses and small radii, which have recently attracted considerable attention in observational studies.

entries.title: How general relativity stacks up: Testing gravity by coherently combining gravitational-wave observations
entries.abstract: A core mission of gravitational-wave astronomy is to test general relativity (GR) in the high-curvature, high-velocity regime. The field has already seen significant progress in this space, though a remaining challenge is how to combine data from a population of binary mergers. This can both boost the significance of potential GR violations, and develop a phenomenological picture of how deviations manifest in different mergers. We propose a framework to coherently combine gravitational-wave measurements to build a population-level test of physics beyond GR. We assume that deviations from GR are (i) strongest near the merger, (ii) vary smoothly with the total mass of the binary, and (iii) are most prominent in the $\ell=|m|=2$ mode. While these assumptions do not describe every possible deviation of GR, they provide us with a plausible starting point upon which a more general framework can be built. We apply our framework to 28 high signal-to-noise ratio binary black hole mergers from LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA's Fifth Gravitational-Wave Transient Catalog, finding no evidence for deviations from GR. Our framework allows one to show how deviations could vary as a function of total mass of the system. We argue that such a reconstruction can be used to convincingly distinguish between systematic waveform errors and genuine GR violations.

entries.title: General Relativistic Simulations of the Nonlinear Evolution of r-modes in Rapidly Rotating Neutron Stars
entries.abstract: The r-modes in rotating neutron stars are a promising source of continuous gravitational waves, and may grow or be excited to amplitudes $α\lesssim1$. We perform general relativistic simulations of nonlinear $l=|m|=2$ r-modes in a rapidly rotating neutron star with spin frequency $f_{spin}\approx792$ Hz, relaxing the Cowling and small-$α$ approximations. The star is idealised as an unmagnetised, one-component, perfect fluid with a polytropic equation of state. The r-mode frequency is measured to be $f_{r-mode}=1014$ Hz for initial amplitude $α_0=0.2$. The dimensionless frequency $κ\approx0.7197$ agrees with an estimate from linear perturbation theory to within 1.7%. $f_{r-mode}$ increases quadratically with amplitude, and $κ$ decreases by 3.4% across simulations where $α_0$ is varied through the range $0.2\leqα_0\leq1.2$. The gravitational wave strain calculated from the Newman-Penrose scalar implies $h_{r-mode}\approx9.7\times10^{-22}$ at $10$ kpc for $α_0=0.2$, which agrees with Einstein's quadrupole formula to within 35%. We also report on nonlinear phenomena observed in our simulations, e.g. differential rotation, amplitude decay, and signatures of nonlinear mode coupling in the spacetime oscillations.

entries.title: B-fields In STar-forming Region Observations (BISTRO): Technical Foundations for Quantitative 450/850 $μ$m JCMT SCUBA-2/POL-2 Polarimetry
entries.abstract: We present five technical validations of SCUBA-2/POL-2 polarimetry on the James Clerk Maxwell Telescope at 450 and 850 $μ$m, using 174 archival fields in 69 molecular cloud regions and subsets appropriate to each test. Extended-source calibration avoids a deterministic shift of $Δβ=-1.05$ in the dust emissivity index $β$ that would result from calibrating extended emission using peak brightness. We modeled Stokes $I$ noise with additive and signal-dependent components. The measured median ratio of surface-brightness noise at 450/850 $μ$m is 25. Independent tests of Stokes $Q,U$ noise support approximately equal additive variances and weak error correlations, providing a basis for propagating polarization uncertainties. Corrections determined for individual fields reduce additive zero-level offsets of order $1$ mJy arcsec$^{-2}$ in the 450 $μ$m Stokes $Q$ and $U$ intensities. The three-step regression leaves a median combined residual amplitude of $0.07$ mJy arcsec$^{-2}$. Independent comparisons with SOFIA/HAWC+ at 154 and 214 $μ$m support the correction in strongly affected fields. We matched the 450 $μ$m maps to the modeled 850 $μ$m beam and the common $12.6''$-$300''$ range of angular scales. We compared three reductions of the same 450 $μ$m observations across 30 sources. Taking the median angular residual relative to the final product for each source, we find that beam matching reduces the median over sources from $6.3^\circ$ to $4.7^\circ$. After matching, 29 of the 30 sources have median residuals below $10^\circ$. We also quantified how residual $Q/U$ offsets propagate in ratios of polarization fractions, differences in spectral indices, and polarization angles. These validations provide procedures and quantitative references for interpreting POL-2 measurements and combining them with polarimetry at other wavelengths.

entries.title: B-fields In STar-forming Region Observations (BISTRO): Dual-Wavelength Constraints on Size-Dependent Grain Alignment in Star-Forming Regions
entries.abstract: We compared 450 and 850 $μ$m POL-2 observations from the James Clerk Maxwell Telescope at $12.6''$ resolution. The median absolute difference in polarization angle between bands is $6.7^\circ$ across 21 regions. For total intensity $I\proptoν^α$ and polarized intensity $PI\proptoν^γ$, 24-27 of 35 regions have $γ<α$, allowing for $3σ$ limits on weak polarized intensities. The median $γ-α$ is $-0.51$, ranging from $-0.57$ to $-0.45$ under these limits. The ratio of polarization fractions is $P_{450}/P_{850}=0.69\pm0.02_{\rm sys}\pm0.03_{\rm stat}$, with no detected dependence on the angle difference. We suggest that the dependence of alignment on grain size offers the simplest explanation of these findings. For optically thin components sharing a polarization angle and opacity law, temperature mixing reproduces the median $-0.51$ only if the warm dust is polarized less efficiently than the cold dust. If the cold dust is at 10 K or warmer and the warm dust at 40 K or cooler, the median requires a ratio of warm to cold effective polarization efficiencies $r\lesssim0.18$. We tested mixtures with opacity index $β=2$ in four fields against Herschel dust temperatures and Green Bank Ammonia Survey kinetic temperatures. We assumed equal gas and dust temperatures, ammonia tracing cold gas, and model ranges of 3-20 K for cold dust and 25-40 K for warm dust carrying at most half the mass. Mixtures matching both temperatures cannot reproduce $γ-α$ within $1σ$ in three fields, including OMC 2 tentatively, even for $r=0$. Allowing warm dust at 10-100 K and up to 95% of the mass permits solutions only for $r\leq0.041$. To explain these three fields by temperature mixing, we need wider model ranges and a very strong contrast in polarization efficiency. The origin of this contrast remains undetermined.

entries.title: Enhanced Mass Transfer from Extended Shock-Supported Stellar Chromospheres
entries.abstract: Mass transfer (MT) in binary systems is a crucial and complex process. Even before the donor's photosphere fills its Roche lobe, matter from its outer atmosphere can reach the inner Lagrange point, thus initiating interaction in the so-called optically thin phase. Most existing models account for a very tenuous atmosphere supported by thermal gas pressure, thus predicting very little MT until the donor fills its Roche lobe. However, recent hydrodynamic simulations of giant stars suggest that shock-driven outflows can create substantially thicker "chromospheres'' extending to a few stellar radii. In this work, we derive a simple analytic model for a shock-supported chromosphere in a binary potential and calculate the corresponding MT rate. We also implement our prescription in the stellar evolution code MESA. We show that chromospheric MT rates can be orders of magnitude higher than prior estimates for optically thin MT, especially for stars high on the red giant or asymptotic giant branch. This allows for substantial accretion before Roche lobe overflow, both for systems that undergo stable mass transfer and for systems that go through common envelope evolution. Thus, for a given initial binary configuration, this may alter the final period and component masses compared to those predicted classically. Our model is similar to Wind Roche-lobe Overflow, but it is physically rather than empirically motivated. We discuss implications for various post-interaction binaries that can be tested with population synthesis studies and observed binary populations. Additionally, we have identified an inaccuracy in the current implementation of the optically-thin Ritter 1988 prescription in MESA, which we correct.

entries.title: simesh: A Python Framework for Quantitative Analysis of Native AMR Data from MPI-AMRVAC
entries.abstract: Adaptive mesh refinement (AMR) is widely used in large-scale astrophysical simulations, but the resulting multilevel data are challenging to analyze quantitatively. We present simesh, an independent Python framework for quantitative analysis of cell-centered fields on block-structured AMR meshes.
